title: Groupoïdes de Teichmüller et les S0 Tg,!ν, S0 TG : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This is a working page from a calculation that turns a groupoid or group presentation into relations purely among 'edge' generators. Grothendieck has three families of elements, ã_r, b̃_r and c̃_r, indexed by r in a set R. The index r has successors written r', r''. There are also 'monodromy' elements μ attached to two kinds of cells: Q̃ (indexed by a ∈ A, with a base cell Q̃_0) and R̃_r (indexed by r). A superscript ω marks a choice of base point or starting flag ω.

The boxed defining relations are:
- (3) μ_{R̃_r}∘b̃_r = b̃_{r'}∘μ_{Q̃_a}^ω.
- (4) μ_{R̃_{r'}}∘ã_r = ã_{r'}∘μ_{R̃_r}.
- (2) μ_{Q̃_a}^ω c̃_r = c̃_{r'} d̃_{ωr^n}⋯d̃_{r''}.
Relation (1) is referred to but not shown on this page.

Using (1), μ_{Q̃_0} is written as an ordered product around a cycle, Ã_{ωr^n}⋯Ã_{ωr'}Ã_{r''}, with Ã_r = b̃_r^{-1}ã_r^{-1}b̃_{r'}. Substituting into (3) gives μ_{R̃_r} as a product B̃_{ωr^n}⋯B̃_{ωr}B̃_r, with B̃_r := ã_{r''}^{-1}b̃_{r'}b̃_r^{-1}.

This is a Tietze-type elimination: the μ's are expressed through the edge generators and then removed. Relation (4) then becomes a relation among ã, b̃, c̃ alone. To it one must add that the expression of μ_{Q̃_0} does not depend on the choice of starting point ω along the cycle (μ_{Q̃_0}^{ω_i} = μ_{Q̃_0}).

The right-hand column notes that this gives two groups of relations among ã_r, b̃_r, c̃_r, those in which the μ's are eliminated:
- one group indexed by a ∈ A (base-point independence);
- one group indexed by r ∈ R (followed by relation (5)).
Grothendieck then remarks that 'these two relations are equivalent and more or less trivial'.

The last paragraph reorganises the bookkeeping:
- (5) is taken as the definition of λ_{p̃_0^ω};
- (6) and (7) as definitions of λ_{Q̃_0} and λ_{R̃_r} in terms of ã_r, b̃_r, c̃_r;
- so (8) and (9) become equations in ã_r, b̃_r, c̃_r alone.
The λ's look like the images of generators under some morphism or automorphism, or a 'lifting' datum. The page would then be reducing the conditions for such a datum to equations on a small set of edge-level parameters. This is reminiscent, structurally, of reducing an action on a Teichmüller-type tower to equations on a few parameters. However, the page is too fragmentary to identify the cell complex (flags of a map? pants/'maquette' decomposition?) or what λ acts on.

The sheet is recycled paper; the neighbouring sheets are a calculus handout and a 2 March 1978 council attendance sheet, consistent with the '[à partir de 1978]' dating.
errors: No outright mathematical error can be verified, because the setting (relation (1), relations (5)–(9)) is not on the page. The claim that the two relation groups are 'equivalent and ± trivial' is asserted, not proved, here.

Index bookkeeping is loose. (4) uses μ_{R̃_{r'}} on the left and μ_{R̃_r} on the right, while the derived product for μ_{R̃_r} starts at B̃_r. Consistency of the successor maps r↦r', r'' cannot be checked from this page alone.

ideas.what: Eliminating cell-monodromy generators μ (Tietze transformation) to get a presentation by edge generators ã, b̃, c̃ only, with μ written as ordered products around a cycle
ideas.modern_name: Tietze transformations / presentation of a fundamental groupoid from a 2-complex (cellular presentation)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses generators-and-relations presentations of Teichmüller groupoids in general terms only

ideas.what: Requiring that the product expression of a cycle monodromy be independent of the starting point ω (cyclic-conjugation invariance)
ideas.modern_name: base-point independence / cyclic invariance of boundary words

ideas.what: Treating some relations as definitions of auxiliary data λ, so that the remaining conditions become equations on the parameters ã, b̃, c̃
ideas.modern_name: reduction of an action or lifting to parameter equations (structurally like reducing GT-type actions to equations on a few parameters)
ideas.usually_credited_to: for GT: Drinfeld (1990), Ihara; the identification here is speculative

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine, fragmentary elimination computation in a combinatorial presentation, with crossed-out attempts. The underlying objects cannot be identified from the page, and nothing visible goes beyond standard Tietze and base-point bookkeeping.
transcription_corrections: In (3) the right-hand side reads μ_{Q̃_a}^ω (superscript ω), not μ_{Q̃_a}^a.
In the boxed relation (2) the superscript on μ_{Q̃_a} is ω, not °.
The arrow target after (2) is likely 'R_r' or a reference to the R-relations, not 'R_x'.
'fluide fibre' under the crossed-out box is uncertain. The phrase 'indép. de ...' written above (3) is linked to the later remark on independence of the expression of μ_{Q̃_0}.
Right-column text: 'et (4) devient une relation entre les ã_r, b̃_r, c̃_r, à laquelle il faut ajouter l'indépendance de l'expression de μ_{Q̃_0} p.r. à ω'.
Left-column text: 'relation a ∈ A (μ_{Q̃_0}^{ω_i}=μ_{Q̃_0}) ou r ∈ R (suivie de la relation (5))'.
Right margin: 'Mais on voit que ces deux relations sont équivalentes et ± triviales'.
The number 28 at the bottom left is the archive page number.
